title: autocomplete_for has no honeypot guard; greedy suffix/exact matching can tokenize it
detail: autocomplete_for pattern-matches names with no honeypot exemption. A honeypot whose name ends in _name/_email/_phone/_employer (or hits an exact entry) gets a real token, violating the spec's Never and weakening anti-fraud.
recommended_fix: Add an exact-name guard at the top of autocomplete_for returning "off" for the honeypot field name(s) before any suffix/exact matching. Don't rely on the honeypot name happening to dodge every suffix.

title: Spec's exact-table/suffix-rule partition doesn't match code (employer_ref_name, _amount)
evidence: Spec task: `exact-name table (existing 8 + job_title, employer_name, guarantor_employer, monthly_income_cents, guarantor_monthly_income_cents, employer_ref_name, amount) then suffix rules (_name, _email, _phone, _employer, _monthly_income_cents, _amount)`. Code exact `case inner` block has no `employer_ref_name` arm; code suffix `rules` list is `_monthly_income_cents, _employer, _phone, _email, _name` — no `_amount`.
detail: Spec promises employer_ref_name as an exact entry and _amount as a suffix rule; code omits both (employer_ref_name resolves via _name suffix, amount via exact match). Outputs are still correct; only the implemented structure diverges from the approved spec.
recommended_fix: Align the two: either add employer_ref_name to the exact table and an _amount suffix rule, or update the spec task list to match the implemented partition.
